updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - Aug 2026 Update
updates.html:
Below is the update for Operations in the month of July 2026. This closes out Operating Month 12, the final month of Year 1!

Asset Management Summary

On a trailing-3-month basis, NOI annualizes to $149,445, which is 54% ahead of the Year 1 pro forma of $96,867. On a full-year basis, T-12 NOI annualizes to $130,165, 34% ahead of plan. Both revenue and expenses contributed: EGI came in 33% above pro forma while operating expenses ran 11% below.

Average rent per occupied unit is $805, up 15.7% since acquisition. Occupancy averaged 99.5% for the period, closing July at 100% (zero vacant units), and both August turns were pre-leased before the units went vacant.

At a trailing-3 valuation the property is worth $2,134,929, which puts the implied LP equity multiple at 1.88x on paper. That is a valuation mark, not a realized figure.

Distributions

LP distributions paid to date total $18,188, a 3.75% cash-on-cash return for Year 1 against a 3.92% target. On $100,000 invested, that is $3,750 returned so far.

Financial & Tax Updates

July NOI was $13,014 against a pro forma of $8,072, a 61% variance. Two things drove it: revenue held at $17,714 on full occupancy, and it was a quiet repair month, with R&M at $260 versus $821 in June. Operating expenses totaled $4,701.

Cash reserves stand at $48,139. The loan balance is $1,020,568, with $1,466 of principal paid down this month and $14,432 retired since acquisition.

Leasing & Revenue

  • Unit 12 re-leased at $900 plus $45 RUBS, up from $695. Move-in 7/20.
  • Unit 2 re-leased at $900 plus $45 RUBS, up from $757. Move-in 7/27.
  • Unit 3 vacated 7/31. Backfill already signed at $900 plus $45 RUBS plus $30 pet rent.
  • Unit 7 gave a lease break and is out 8/4. Backfill already signed at $900 plus $45 RUBS plus $30 internet.
  • Both August turns were leased before the units emptied, so there is no foregone rent on either one.
  • Year 1 finished with 10 move-outs and 0.9% vacancy (59 total days) across all turns.

Rent Collection

Rent collection ran 99.3% on a trailing-3-month basis and 99.8% across the full year. RUBS collections totaled $835 for the month.

Unit 4 remains $435 past due and is on a payment arrangement. I am watching it closely. All other tenants paid as expected.

Operations & Maintenance

  • I found three units that had never opened their own PG&E accounts, which meant the property had been absorbing those meters. Electricity expense ran $278 in July versus $129 in June as a result.
  • We corrected this with PG&E and transferred service to the residents. Utility expense should normalize in August.
  • Two of the three residents have reimbursed their back billings.

Capital Expenditures

We are installing a dedicated fiber line into the maintenance closet in the laundry shed. Service runs $65 per month with the first three months free, and we spent $1,100 on a router and two access points to cover the full building. The network is provisioned with pre-shared private keys, so each unit runs on its own isolated virtual network rather than a shared wifi connection.

Unit 7's new lease is the first subscriber at $30 per month. We are adding it as leases turn and renew rather than pushing it to existing residents mid-lease, so adoption will be gradual. Three subscribers covers the monthly service cost, and equipment payback accelerates from there. At full building adoption, the plan contributes roughly $535 per month, or $6,420 per year, net of service cost. That is a multi-year target, not a near-term number.

Forward Look

  • August begins Operating Year 2. The annual insurance renewal (roughly $14,864) hits in August and is the single largest cash item of the year.
  • Attach the $30 internet plan to every new lease and renewal going forward.
  • Collect the remaining PG&E back bill.

Year 1 came in ahead of plan on nearly every line that matters, and I appreciate you being part of it. Always available if you want to dig into any of the numbers above.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - July 2026 Update
updates.html:
Below is the update for Operations in the month of June 2026.

Asset Management Summary

On a trailing three-month basis, NOI annualizes to $147,272, which is 52% ahead of the Year 1 pro forma of $96,867. The trailing twelve months annualize to $127,884 (32% ahead of plan), so the most recent quarter is running well above even the full-year pace. The outperformance comes from two places: revenue is ahead on strong occupancy (98.8%) and rent growth, and operating expenses are running about 6% under budget.

Rents are up 13.2% since acquisition. Using the trailing-three-month NOI, the implied property value is $2,103,883 and the LP equity multiple on paper is 1.81x.

Distributions

Distributions total 2.50% cash-on-cash to date, or $2,500 per $100,000 invested. The next quarterly distribution, funded from operating cash flow, will be paid on July 1 at 1.25% for the quarter ($1,250 per $100,000), bringing cumulative distributions to 3.75%.

Looking ahead, our cash flow projections show the property could sustain an 8.5% cash-on-cash distribution. If that holds over the next couple of quarters, we plan to raise the monthly cash distributions accordingly.

Financial & Tax Updates

June NOI came in at $12,199 against a pro forma of $8,072. The month ran on the same drivers as the run-rate: full occupancy on the revenue side and expenses under budget, with no unusual one-time items. Cash reserves stand at $46,951. The loan paid down another $929 in principal this month ($12,966 since acquisition), so equity is building through both value and amortization.

Leasing & Revenue

  • Unit 1 re-leased at $900, up from $750, a 20% increase. The turn was quick, with the unit vacant about a week (June 11 to 17).
  • Four units are turning over the next several weeks, and we are staying ahead of each one:
    • Unit 2 is vacating July 27, new lease signed at $900 for a same-day July 27 move-in, so zero days vacant and no foregone rent.
    • Unit 3 gave notice (out July 31), marketing now.
    • Unit 7 is breaking its lease (out August 4), marketing now.
    • Unit 12 gave notice (out July 17), backfill already signed at $900 for a July 20 move-in.
  • Every backfill is coming in at $900, above the current $788 average rent, so each turn is lifting the rent roll. One resident has been letting us walk prospects through her occupied unit to pre-lease ahead of turns, which is a real help in keeping vacancy down, and I sent her a small thank-you gift basket.

Rent Collection

  • Average rent per occupied unit is $788, with $845 in RUBS collected for the month. Collections continue to run clean, at 99.2% over the trailing three months and 99.8% over the trailing twelve.
  • Outstanding A/R is just $390. All other tenants paid as expected.

Operations & Maintenance

  • Unit 1 turn: I billed the prior tenant $334.74 for a broken toilet tank lid plus cleaning, so those turn costs were recovered rather than absorbed.
  • One tenant lockout this month, handled as a courtesy at no charge.

Forward Look

  • Pay the July 1 distribution (1.25% cash-on-cash).
  • Close out the Unit 12 and Unit 2 backfills (move-ins July 20 and July 27).
  • Market Units 3 and 7 to keep vacancy minimal through their turns (move out July 31 and August 4).

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - June 2026 Update
updates.html:
Below is the update for Bidwell Cherry 20, reflecting May operations.

Asset Management Summary

On a trailing-3-month basis, NOI annualizes to $147,432, which is 52% ahead of the Year 1 pro forma of $96,867. That gap is coming from both sides: revenue is running about 26% above plan on near-full occupancy, and operating expenses are about 14% under budget. Rents are up 12.1% since acquisition. At the current run-rate, the implied property value is about $2,106,172, which puts the LP equity multiple at 1.81x on paper.

Distributions

To date, LP distributions total a 2.50% cash-on-cash return (that's $2,500 back on every $100,000 invested). That figure looks light against the 3.92% Year 1 target, but it's a timing story, not a performance one. We didn't distribute at acquisition, skipped Q3 2025 while early capital projects were funded ($23,171 in capex year-to-date), and made our first distribution in January 2026 for Q4 2025.

The property is distributing at a 5% annualized rate, ahead of the Year 1 target. The to-date number simply hasn't caught up yet because of the slower start.

Financial & Tax Updates

NOI for May came in at $12,301 against a plan of $8,072, about 52% ahead. The month benefited from full occupancy on the revenue side and operating expenses landing under budget ($4,536 vs. $5,271 planned).

Cash reserves stand at $40,270.

Leasing & Revenue

  • Unit 1: notice received for a 6/15 move-out, now listed at $900. We had four showings (two on 5/20, two on 5/27) and expect a prospect to sign next week.
  • Unit 2: 60-day notice received 5/27 for a 7/27 move-out. One of the Unit 1 prospects may take Unit 2 for an 8/1 move-in.
  • Unit 10 (renovated): the tenant gave notice on 5/3 for family reasons. I let them move out early on the condition they covered rent until I re-leased, so there was no income gap. The unit was listed 5/5, signed 5/16, and the new tenant moved in 5/17 at $1,250 (flat to the prior rent). The new tenant paid three months upfront in place of pay stubs and added $30/month in pet rent.
  • Unit 7: the tenant needs to break their lease early to move back home. They've been straightforward about it and understand they're responsible for rent until the unit is re-leased, and they've offered to send qualified prospects our way for screening. I agreed to that and told them I'd also fill the space through our own marketing if I can (we're showing another unit now, so any extra applicants could backfill Unit 7). No income gap here, the tenant covers rent until we re-lease.

Rent Collection

RUBS collected for the month was $946, and average rent per occupied unit is $780. Collections have held at 100% over the trailing twelve months. Current A/R is $938.

Unit 4 owes $838 and Unit 9 owes $100. All other tenants paid as expected.

Operations & Maintenance

  • Unit 16 turn: after the 4/30 move-out, the unit was in good shape, just a faulty bathroom light and some minor cleaning. The crew replaced the light fixture and finished cleaning on 5/13, ahead of the 5/15 move-in.

Forward Look

  • Sign a new lease on Unit 1 ahead of the 6/15 move-out to keep vacancy near zero.
  • Continue marketing Unit 2 for an 8/1 fill following the 7/27 move-out.
  • Re-lease Unit 7 following the tenant's early lease break, either through a prospect they refer or our own marketing (tenant covers rent until we fill it).
  • Watch Unit 14, where the tenant has signaled a move but hasn't given formal notice yet.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - May 2026 Update
updates.html:
Below is the May 2026 update for Bidwell Cherry 20, reflecting April operations.

Quick note before the update: I've adjusted the format of these reports to give you clearer asset management metrics (variance vs pro forma, trailing performance, implied value) alongside the operational detail you're used to. I'd genuinely value your feedback. If something's unclear, missing, or not landing for you, please tell me - these updates will keep evolving based on what's most useful.

Asset Management Summary

The property continues to run well ahead of underwriting.

NOI this month came in at $12,395 against a pro forma of $8,072, 54% above pro forma. On a trailing-3-month basis, NOI annualizes to $138,401, which is 43% ahead of the Year 1 pro forma of $96,867. The trailing-12 figure is $123,739, or 28% ahead of plan.

Operations are running 17% under budget on expenses, and revenue is 26% above plan, which is what's driving the NOI outperformance. The implied property value based on the T-3 run-rate is $1,977,154.

Distributions

Distributions total $12,125 to date (2.50% cash-on-cash, 3.33% annualized). That's a touch below the 3.92% Year 1 target because we've funded ~$19,000 in capex from cash flow. Distributions should step up as capex normalizes.

Financial & Tax Updates

April NOI of $12,395 reflects clean operations with no one-time items. Reserves stand at $28,721.

Loan principal paid down $1,274 this month, with a cumulative paydown of $11,291 since acquisition. Current loan balance is $1,023,709.

Leasing & Revenue

  • Unit 16: the tenant gave notice 4/1 and vacated at the end of the month. The unit was leased for a 5/15 move-in date at $900 plus $45 RUBS, a $175 increase over prior rent. Showings were completed on 4/14, which kept the turn tight.

Rent Collection

EGI for the month was $16,770, including $842 in RUBS. A/R sits at $693, which I'm watching but not concerned about at this level. All other tenants paid as expected.

Operations & Maintenance

Unit 10

  • Small kitchen sink leak on 4/17. We replaced the tail piece and resolved it the same day. I ordered a metal-threaded sink drain to replace the plastic original.
  • The fan light cable had been wrapped around the fan. Corrected.

Unit 19

  • Toilet clog cleared 4/22 and drain replaced. We used the snake we had previously purchased.
  • Ordered a replacement for the leaky shower faucet.

Capital Expenditures

Capex YTD is $19,365. No new material projects to flag this month.

Forward Look

  • Complete Unit 16 turn (cleaning and touch-up) ahead of the 5/15 move-in.
  • Install the Unit 19 shower faucet replacement once the parts arrive.
  • Continue pushing rent increases on rollover, with a target $900 per month rate.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - Jan 2026 Update
updates.html:
I hope you all had a great end to the year. Below is the update covering December operations, maintenance items, unit turns, and financial activity.

Rent & Collections

  • Unit 4 was late again due to the tenant being between jobs. December rent has now been paid in full, and the tenant has indicated that January will be paid on time.
  • All other units paid on time.

Maintenance & Operations

  • Unit 17: tenant reported an odor believed to be a plumbing issue. When I looked at the fridge, there seemed to be no issue. As a courtesy, we swapped the refrigerator with a lightly used unit and placed the existing one into storage after inspection.
  • December 24 sewer backup impacting Units 5 & 6:
    • An initial jetting attempt was unsuccessful.
    • We called Accurate Plumbing, who removed a significant root intrusion but did not solve the issue. Blockage between Unit 6 and the main line persisted.
    • During troubleshooting, a toilet in Unit 5 was accidentally damaged and immediately replaced (at no cost to us).
    • We purchased a professional-grade drain snake (~$600) and successfully cleared the line ourselves on Dec 26.
    • Going forward, we will perform quarterly preventative drain cleanings to manage root intrusion in the older sewer lines.

Unit Rehab - Unit 10

  • Unit 10 vacated on December 15. We are fully rehabbing the unit in an attempt to push rents to the top of the market.
  • Work completed: plumbing updates, floor leveling and new flooring, electrical reconfiguration, interior layout improvements, new drywall, fully tiled shower, mini-split installed, paint complete, cabinets mostly installed.
  • Remaining work: finish cabinets, counters and trim, final touch-up paint.
  • Minor ceiling damage in Unit 9 during rehab was repaired.
  • Expected to list this unit in the first half of January.
  • Estimated rehab cost: $15,000-$20,000 (final accounting pending).

Upcoming Vacancy

  • Unit 20 will vacate on January 31. Listing this week.
  • Target rent: ~$850 + RUBS.

Cost Segregation

  • Cost segregation study completed.
  • $419,340 Year 1 deduction, approximately 86% of total investment.

Distributions

  • Distribution initiated: 1.25% cash-on-cash (a $100,000 investment receives a $1,250 distribution).
  • Paid from net operating profits since acquisition, which includes having funded the cost segregation study (~$4,500) and Unit 10 rehab (~$15,000).
  • Expectation: targeting 1.25% quarterly (5% annualized) after Q1. Q2 distributions to be reassessed based on performance.

January Priorities

  • Complete Unit 10 rehab and lease.
  • Lease Unit 20.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - Nov 2025 Update
updates.html:
It's been a steady month at Cherry Street. We wrapped up maintenance on a few units and handled some unexpected repairs. Leasing remains strong with a smooth tenant transition in progress. The cost segregation study is underway, with solid depreciation benefits expected.

Leasing & Occupancy

  • Unit 6: tenant moved out a few days early; new tenant moves in 11/1.
  • Outgoing tenant will receive most of their deposit back (less charges for a broken towel bar, window blind, and cleaning).
  • Painter completed touch-ups, and we replaced a broken bathroom fan.
  • All other units remain occupied.

Maintenance & Repairs

  • Unit 15: replaced kitchen ceiling light, fixed flooring gaps, replaced P-trap, and repaired toilet valve leak. Rebuilt shower curb with new tile.
  • Mailbox lockout: locksmith serviced due to no spare key; cost $120, tenant billed $200.
  • Water leak: mid-month, a shower hot water line failed and soaked the surrounding drywall. Replaced kitchen-side drywall, dried other areas, replaced the shower valve, added shut-offs, and repainted. Total cost: ~$1,000.

Capital Improvements & Materials

  • Purchased a 20" stove and above-counter microwave from one of my STR clients for $500 total (roughly half of retail).
  • The seller also included a shower base pan, which we'll use in our first rehab.

Cost Segregation Study

  • Cost segregation has been negotiated down to $4,000 and paid.
  • Report expected early January.
  • Estimated bonus depreciation: 60% to 80% of the amount invested.

Income & Financials

  • First laundry income check received: $106.51 for the month.
  • Maintenance costs were slightly elevated due to the water leak and bathroom rebuild, but overall expenses remain on track.
  • Current reserves remain stable, and we are closing out the month with $37,000 in the account.

Overall, things are going well. We're continuing to refine maintenance systems, improve unit conditions, and prepare for upcoming rehabs that will allow us to push rents and overall property value further.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - October 2025 Update
updates.html:

Overall, we're in a strong position going into Q4, with full occupancy secured, the capital raise completed, and reserves in place.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - September 2025 Update
updates.html:
I'm excited to share our first full post-closing update with you on the Bidwell Cherry 20 deal:

  • Closed on August 21, 2025. Title and funding are complete.
  • Capital Raise: we're still bringing in the final $100K, and I'll keep you posted as that wraps up.
  • Insurance: there was a miscommunication with the insurance agent regarding flood coverage - it was not included in the original quote, even though I requested it. We've corrected this, and while it does not significantly change the overall deal, it does reduce the Year 1 cash-on-cash return by about 1%. To offset this, I'm deferring $4,900 of my loan guarantee fee to a future date so that investors don't absorb the impact.
  • Financing: good news here - the loan came in better than expected. Originally quoted at 6.75%, we locked in a 6.25% fixed rate for 5 years.

Property Management Transition

We gave the existing property manager a 30-day notice, and they chose to quit the next day. Given their lackluster track record, conversations that didn't inspire confidence, and their attempt to increase the fee to 10%, I believe this worked out in our favor.

Management is now in-house. So far:

  • Most of the tenants have already set up online accounts, and the rest have committed to doing so soon.
  • Most tenants have signed new leases, and we successfully implemented RUBS at $45 per unit on 18 of the 20 units.
  • A handful of deferred maintenance issues were brought up by tenants. Some have already been resolved, and the remainder are scheduled for next month per tenant requests.
  • Utilities are set up.
  • Trash service is $260/month.
  • Landscaping is $160/month for weekly service.
  • I'm currently getting a pest control quote, but the ballpark was $110/month with the first month being $250 due to the lack of prior maintenance.

Rent Growth Plan

  • The next vacant unit will be listed at $850 + $45 RUBS, testing the market at a higher level.
  • The second vacant unit will receive a full renovation (new kitchen, new bath, new floor plan). We'll also add Quiet Board and Green Glue to the walls to reduce sound transfer between units, improving long-term tenant satisfaction and value.

Distributions

Once the final investment is funded, I will start doing quarterly distributions. There will not be a Q3 distribution; however, I do plan on doing a distribution in January for Q4.

Reporting

Starting next month, I'll provide monthly P&L reports. These will always have a one-month lag since investor emails go out on the 1st, and it takes a few weeks to close books. Expect the August P&L in the October 1st email.

updates.title: Bidwell Cherry 20 - First Update & Final $100K Raise
updates.html:
This is the first investor update for the 946 Cherry St Apartment deal, and I'm excited to share some good news and a few updates as we move toward closing.

Quick Highlights

  • We've raised $400K of the $500K and have funds in the bank.
  • We are scheduled to close on August 15th.
  • The appraisal just came back at $1.6M, which is $100K over our purchase price - great confirmation that we're walking into equity from day one.
